headline_marked: BNP to name candidate today; [[Mirza Fakhrul likely presidential nominee]]
headline: BNP to name candidate today; Mirza Fakhrul likely presidential nominee
summary: BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman will finalize the candidate after a Standing Committee meeting today, with Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir seen as the frontrunner.
details: BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman is set to meet with the party's Standing Committee today to make a final decision on the party's presidential candidate. Following the meeting, the party will submit nomination papers to the Election Commission around 12:30 PM.
Today is the deadline for filing nominations. According to the Election Commission's schedule, papers must be submitted between 10:00 AM and 4:00 PM.
Multiple party sources indicate that BNP Secretary General and LGRD Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is likely to be nominated for the presidency.
The party's Chief Whip, Nurul Islam Moni, stated that the BNP will submit its nomination paper after Jamaat-e-Islami files theirs, after which the candidate's name will be publicly announced.
Voting for the presidential election will take place on August 20 during a parliamentary sitting, where lawmakers will cast their votes via an open ballot.
The presidential post became vacant after Md Shahabuddin resigned on July 24, with Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed currently serving as acting president.
If Mirza Fakhrul is nominated and wins, the government will need to determine successors for his current roles as LGRD minister, lawmaker, and BNP secretary general.
caption:
Mirza Fakhrul is likely to be the BNP's presidential candidate. The final decision will be announced today.

BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman is set to meet with the party's Standing Committee today to make a final decision on the party's presidential candidate. Following the meeting, the party will submit nomination papers to the Election Commission around 12:30 PM.

Today is the deadline for filing nominations. According to the Election Commission's schedule, papers must be submitted between 10:00 AM and 4:00 PM.

Multiple party sources indicate that BNP Secretary General and LGRD Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is likely to be nominated for the presidency.

The party's Chief Whip, Nurul Islam Moni, stated that the BNP will submit its nomination paper after Jamaat-e-Islami files theirs, after which the candidate's name will be publicly announced.

Voting for the presidential election will take place on August 20 during a parliamentary sitting, where lawmakers will cast their votes via an open ballot.

The presidential post became vacant after Md Shahabuddin resigned on July 24, with Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed currently serving as acting president.

If Mirza Fakhrul is nominated and wins, the government will need to determine successors for his current roles as LGRD minister, lawmaker, and BNP secretary general.

headline_marked: Hasan Mahmud takes 6 wickets, [[Bangladesh bundle Australia out for 198]]
headline: Hasan Mahmud takes 6 wickets, Bangladesh bundle Australia out for 198
summary: Pacer Hasan Mahmud becomes the first Bangladeshi bowler to take a fifer in Australia, leading the Tigers to a dominant Day 1 performance.
details: Pacer Hasan Mahmud made history by becoming the first Bangladeshi bowler to take a five-wicket haul in Australia, finishing with career-best figures of 6 for 55 in 17 overs.
The Tigers bundled out the hosts for 198 in 53 overs on Day 1 of the first Test at Marrara Stadium in Darwin.
Hasan's dominant spell included removing the well-set Steve Smith (71) and Nathan Lyon, claiming the final two wickets after tea.
Bangladesh's three pacers claimed all 10 Australian wickets, with Taskin Ahmed and Ebadot Hossain contributing two wickets each.
Australia's innings was characterized by relentless pressure from the Tigers' pace attack, which exposed the Australian tail.
Steve Smith was the lone recognized batter to resist, scoring 45th Test fifty, reaching 71 off 109 deliveries.
Earlier in the day, Hasan struck twice in successive overs to reduce Australia to 52-2 after 14 overs.
The performance marks a significant improvement over the previous best by a Bangladeshi bowler in Australia, since Mashrafe Bin Mortaza's 3 for 74 in 2003.
caption:
Hasan Mahmud makes history! 6 wickets for 55 runs as Bangladesh destroys Australia's first innings.

Pacer Hasan Mahmud made history by becoming the first Bangladeshi bowler to take a five-wicket haul in Australia, finishing with career-best figures of 6 for 55 in 17 overs.

The Tigers bundled out the hosts for 198 in 53 overs on Day 1 of the first Test at Marrara Stadium in Darwin.

Hasan's dominant spell included removing the well-set Steve Smith (71) and Nathan Lyon, claiming the final two wickets after tea.

Bangladesh's three pacers claimed all 10 Australian wickets, with Taskin Ahmed and Ebadot Hossain contributing two wickets each.

Australia's innings was characterized by relentless pressure from the Tigers' pace attack, which exposed the Australian tail.

Steve Smith was the lone recognized batter to resist, scoring 45th Test fifty, reaching 71 off 109 deliveries.

Earlier in the day, Hasan struck twice in successive overs to reduce Australia to 52-2 after 14 overs.

The performance marks a significant improvement over the previous best by a Bangladeshi bowler in Australia, since Mashrafe Bin Mortaza's 3 for 74 in 2003.
